items.q: Subword tokenization (BPE/WordPiece) primarily solves…
choices: The open-vocabulary problem: rare words become composable pieces
items.explain: Splitting rare words into known subword pieces gives full vocabulary coverage with a bounded vocabulary — no UNK graveyard.

items.q: The distributional hypothesis behind Word2Vec states…
choices: Words appearing in similar contexts have similar meanings
items.explain: ‘You shall know a word by the company it keeps’ — co-occurrence statistics become geometry.

items.q: In NER evaluation, the standard metric is…
items.explain: Entity recognition is scored on exact spans with correct types — token accuracy is inflated by the easy non-entity majority.

items.q: Beam search decoding, versus greedy decoding,…
choices: Keeps multiple candidate hypotheses to avoid greedy dead ends
items.explain: Beam search tracks k hypotheses; it beats greedy locally-optimal mistakes but still is not globally optimal.

items.q: Removing stopwords before training a modern transformer classifier is…
choices: Usually unnecessary or harmful: subword models use full context
items.explain: Contextual models learn from the full sequence; stopword removal was a bag-of-words-era heuristic that now mostly destroys signal.

items.q: A model card should tell you, at minimum,…
choices: Intended uses, training data, evaluation, and limitations
items.explain: Model cards document purpose, data, metrics, and limits — the minimum due diligence before deploying someone's checkpoint.

items.q: The ReAct pattern interleaves…
choices: Reasoning traces with tool actions and observations
items.explain: ReAct: the model reasons about what to do, acts via a tool, observes the result, and repeats — the loop most agents implement.

items.q: The single biggest operational risk of an autonomous agent loop is…
choices: Unbounded loops: repeated failing actions burning cost and time
items.explain: Without step caps, timeouts, and human checkpoints, agents retry failing actions indefinitely — cost and side effects compound.

items.q: Function-calling schemas serve as…
choices: Machine-readable contracts: name, description, typed parameters the model must fill
items.explain: The schema is the contract: it tells the model exactly what it may call and with what typed arguments.

items.q: Least privilege for agent tools means…
choices: Giving the agent admin to avoid errors
Each tool gets only the permissions its task needs; destructive tools need confirmation
items.explain: An agent with a delete-database tool and no confirmation step is an incident waiting for a misread instruction.

items.q: Copilot Studio's low-code approach trades…
choices: Speed of building against depth of control — governance still required
items.explain: Low-code ships fast for well-scoped tasks; custom logic, evaluation rigor, and data governance still need engineering judgment.

items.q: Evaluating an agent requires, beyond task success,…
choices: Measuring tool-call efficiency, failure recovery, and safety-constraint adherence
items.explain: An agent that succeeds in 40 wasteful, risky steps is worse than one succeeding in 5 safe ones — measure the path, not just the arrival.

items.q: Which Azure AI service converts speech to text?
items.explain: Speech-to-text is Azure AI Speech's transcription capability.

items.q: Azure OpenAI Service differs from OpenAI's public API mainly in…
choices: Enterprise controls: private networking, data residency, Entra ID
items.explain: Same model family; the Azure value is enterprise deployment controls, not different intelligence.

items.q: Anomaly detection on sensor readings with no labeled failures is…
items.explain: No labels means unsupervised: find the unusual patterns without a teacher signal.

items.q: Which principle does ‘the system should work equally well across demographic groups’ express?
items.explain: Fairness: equitable performance and treatment across groups — a core Responsible AI principle.

items.q: Content Safety is used to…
choices: Detect harmful content in text and images
items.explain: Content Safety moderates text/images for hate, violence, sexual, and self-harm categories.

items.q: Document Intelligence is the right choice for…
choices: Extracting structured data from forms and invoices
items.explain: Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) pulls key-value pairs and tables from documents.

items.q: To control spend on AI workloads you should use…
choices: Cost Management + Billing with budgets and alerts
items.explain: Budgets, alerts, and cost analysis in Cost Management are the exam's — and reality's — answer.

items.q: Azure Machine Learning designer is best described as…
choices: A drag-and-drop interface for building ML pipelines
items.explain: The designer offers low-code visual ML pipelines; the SDK/CLI is the pro-code route.

items.q: Data residency requirements are addressed in Azure by…
choices: Choosing regions and services that keep data in required geographies
items.explain: Compliance starts with region choice: data stays where the regulation says it must.

items.q: A regression problem predicts…
items.explain: Regression outputs numbers (prices, temperatures); classification outputs categories.

items.q: Which feature helps ensure a deployed model keeps performing?
choices: Monitoring for data drift and retraining triggers
items.explain: Production data drifts; monitoring plus retraining keeps the model honest after deployment.

items.q: The program labels this material ‘AI-901’; Microsoft's actual fundamentals exam is…
items.explain: Microsoft's exam is AI-900 (Azure AI Fundamentals). Schedule and study from the official certification page, not the program's label.

items.q: The first model you build for a capstone should be…
choices: The simplest credible baseline, to beat deliberately
items.explain: Baselines set the bar and expose data problems cheaply; complexity must earn its place by beating them.

items.q: Error analysis means…
choices: Studying misclassified examples to find patterns and guide the next iteration
Tuning until train error is zero
items.explain: Looking at actual failures reveals whether you need more data, better features, or a different model — tuning blind does not.

items.q: An ablation study tells you…
choices: Which components actually contributed, by removing them
items.explain: Remove each piece and measure the drop: credit assignment for your architecture decisions.

items.q: Data drift in production means…
choices: Input distributions shifted from training, degrading the model
items.explain: The world moves; monitoring input distributions catches the shift before users feel the decay.

items.q: A model card for your capstone should include…
choices: Intended use, data, evaluation, limitations, and ethical notes
items.explain: The card is the honesty layer: what it does, what it was tested on, where it fails.

items.q: The strongest signal to a hiring manager from a capstone is…
choices: A clear problem, honest evaluation with limits stated, and a working demo
items.explain: Perfect accuracy signals leakage or a toy problem; honest evaluation with stated limits signals an engineer.
